title: Bachelor's Grove: The Cemetery in the Woods Outside Chicago

sources.what: first recorded burial 1838; settler families; headstones stolen and thrown into the lagoon; Cook County took over maintenance 1975; the 1991 photo ran in the Sun-Times and Tribune
first burials 1838/1844; last burial 1989; 'few of these tales have any apparent basis in fact' (historian Brad Bettenhausen)
road closed to vehicles since the 1960s; vandalism peaked in the 1970s
Aug. 1991 infrared photo of a woman on a tombstone by Jude Huff-Felz; phantom farmhouse; blue and red lights
the road closed in the 1960s; phantom farmhouse accounts (Richard Crowe); orbs
fewer than two dozen gravestones remain; phantom farmhouse; visit sunrise to sundown

beats.text: Deep in the woods outside Chicago, there's a cemetery the road forgot.
beats.label: NEAR MIDLOTHIAN, ILLINOIS

beats.text: Settlers were burying their dead here by the 1840s, and some say earlier.
beats.label: SINCE THE 1800s

beats.text: In the 1960s, the road beside it closed. Then vandals came, toppling and stealing headstones.
beats.label: FORGOTTEN
beats.credit: Chicago & Cook County Cemeteries; Michael Kleen; WBEZ

beats.text: And the stories spread. Lights drifting between the graves. A farmhouse that appears, then fades away.
beats.label: WHAT PEOPLE REPORT
beats.credit: Ghost Research Society; Michael Kleen; Nature in Chicago

beats.text: In 1991, a ghost hunter's infrared photo seemed to show a woman in an old-fashioned dress, sitting alone on a tombstone.
Most of the gravestones are gone now. The stories never stopped.
beats.label: STILL TOLD

beats.text: It's surrounded by the Rubio Woods forest preserve, open sunrise to sunset. Don't be there after dark.
beats.label: RUBIO WOODS
beats.credit: Forest Preserves of Cook County; Nature in Chicago

beats.text: Comment your town, and it could be next.

factcheck.result: Lines 1, 3, 6 supported. Start date now 'by the 1840s, some say earlier'; 'stories began' became 'spread'; the 1991 woman is in an old-fashioned dress (black-and-white infrared), not 'white'; it's county cemetery land surrounded by the forest preserve; 'near Midlothian'; obelisk and town-house drawings replaced.
